checks.disposition: supported exact counterexample to the all-points height assertion
source_anchors: Definition1.7 p4 and star locus p6
checks.reason: Over Qbar(t), Phi=(z^2,z^2+t) has common degree2, exactly one isotrivial factor, and C:y=1/(x-2) is a smooth irreducible graph with both projections isomorphisms. Non-isotriviality of z^2+t follows from its nonconstant fixed-point multiplier invariant: the finite multipliers have polynomial u^2-2u+4t. Its degree2 also excludes non-isotrivial exceptional flexible Lattes maps. Every image Phi^n(C) has unique second-coordinate-infinite point (2^(2^n),infinity), so these image curves are distinct and C is not preperiodic. The section P_t=(2,infinity) is retained by the stated star locus: a contained horizontal preperiodic multisection has first coordinate preperiodic for z^2, hence0,infinity or a root of unity, never2. Ambient intersections not contained as special components of C are not removed by that definition. For every algebraic t, hhat(P_t)=log2, whereas h_O(1)(t) is unbounded on positive integers. Finite base shrinkage does not help.
checks.counterevidence: This is not a counterexample to the isotrivial-free Theorem1.11. The defective extension uses geometric height-zero implies preperiodic in a coordinate where that implication is false. The example refutes the asserted all-points extension, while the downstream proof needs only generic small sequences.
checks.repair_check: Theorem4.3 gives positive geometric curve height under the dominant mixed/nonconstant-isotrivial cases of4.12. AppendixA.1, on a normal flat model and for fixed ample base bundle N, gives a nonempty dense open height inequality by its explicit bigness/Siu construction. Definition4.11 genericity implies that a fixed proper closed complement contains only finitely many terms. Thus the required base-height bound in4.13 survives after finite deletion. This repairs that use, not the full original star-locus statement; the slope may depend on N.

checks.disposition: supported central proof defect with the report's conditional local replacement verified
source_anchors: Lemma5.2 p26, between5.5 and concluding equality; diagram5.2 p25
checks.reason: For pi(z)=z^2 and mu=(1+epsilon*cos(theta))*Haar with0<epsilon<1, pi_*mu=Haar but pi^*pi_*mu=2Haar differs from2mu. Testing cos(theta) gives0 and epsilon. Positivity and absence of atoms hold. Finiteness alone supplies the opposite-order identity pi_*pi^*nu=deg(pi)nu, not the identity used by the paper. Lemma5.2 is a central input to the slicing proof of1.8 and hence1.4.
checks.counterevidence: The example refutes a general inference; it does not satisfy all dynamical/small-sequence hypotheses of Lemma5.2 and does not refute that lemma or the main relative conclusion. The required symmetry of the actual limiting measure can instead be proved.
checks.repair_check: Set Y=C x_B X, Z=P1 x X and M_i=tildepi_i^* L_i. After allowed base shrinkage, tildepi_i is finite of degree a_i. All data descend to a common number field. Construct the canonical nef L_i on the ambient dynamical family using YZ6.1.1, then restrict to Z; invariance of Z is not required for restriction. Earlier nondegeneracy gives positive geometric degree. The exact projection formula is deg(M_i,Y)=a_i deg(L_i,Z)>0. The same generic sequence on Y has0<=h_Mi(z_n)<=hhat_full(z_n)->0. Nef intersection positivity and YZ5.3.3 then imply0<=h_Mi(Y)<=essential_minimum=0. YZ5.4.3 applies directly on Y to both bundles, so uniqueness of the common normalized orbit-measure limit gives P=(a_i v_i)^(-1)tildepi_i^*nu_i. If c1(L_i)^r=b_i nu_i, the geometric degree is b_i v_i and b_i cancels from the normalized measure; no unexplained literal identification of v_i with a differently normalized degree is needed. Proper pushforward through the Cartesian square commutes with finite pullback off the branch locus. Continuous-potential top Green products do not charge its proper analytic preimage, extending the equality across branching. Consequently pi1^*p_*nu1=(a1 v1)/(a2 v2) pi2^*p_*nu2. This is a complete local replacement conditional on the earlier positive-degree inputs and cited adelic theory.

checks.disposition: supported failure of the extra unequal-degree assertion
checks.reason: On the diagonal C, both projections have degree1. The maps z^2 and z^3 have the same atomless balanced Haar probability measure on S1, so the asserted normalized equality and support intersection hold. No positive ell,k solve2^ell=3^k. The statement expressly allows unequal degrees; exceptional torus cosets do not imply the asserted commensurability.
checks.counterevidence: Theorem1.10 imposes equal degrees, and the later test-function application uses that equal-degree result. This example therefore does not invalidate the principal equal-degree chain.
checks.repair_check: Separate an ordinary commensurate-iterate alternative from the exceptional coset alternative. The printed log-plus equality also fails on xy=1 at (2,1/2). On C-star the correct difference log+|t|-log+|t^-1|=log|t| is harmonic, so equality of dd^c follows there and extends across0,infinity because the measures have no atoms. More generally a coset (a t^m,b t^n) pulls Haar measures to masses |m| and |n| on circles of radii |a|^(-1/m), |b|^(-1/n); intersecting supports force the radii to coincide and yield the normalized equality. A completely rewritten general theorem is not certified.

checks.disposition: supported false conjugacy inference with local fixed-pair repair
checks.reason: Take M_t(z)=z+t, f_t=(z+t)^2-t and g_t=(z+t)^2+1-t. Both maps vary, but their conjugates are z^2 and z^2+1, and (M_t,M_t)(Delta)=Delta is constant. The second map is ordinary, since its critical orbit0,1,2,5,26,... is infinite. The diagonal is not preperiodic: all its image curves project dominantly, while the orbit of(1,1) would place infinitely many distinct points with first coordinate1 in a finite union of such image curves if the curve orbit were finite.
checks.counterevidence: This is not a counterexample to Theorem1.3. Simultaneous conjugacy identifies the common-preperiodic intersection with one fixed pair and leaves its cardinality unchanged.
checks.repair_check: Add the omitted case in which the transformed diagonal is constant and apply the fixed-pair dynamical/classical Manin-Mumford conclusion, with its cited hypotheses. The varying-curve branch then retains the stated separate argument; no impossible-constancy assertion is needed.
